marketPulse: Full Rebound: S&P 500 and Nasdaq at New Records. Memory AI Confirmed. AMD Blows Out AH. Iran Truce Holds.
marketPulseSubtext: S&P 500 +0.81% to 7,259.22 (new record), Nasdaq +1.03% to 25,326.13 (new record), Dow +0.73% to 49,298.25, Russell 2000 +1.75% to 2,845.00 — full reversal of Monday's Iran-driven selloff. Micron +11% on shipping the world's highest-capacity SSD; Intel +13% on Apple chip supply report; AMD +4% AH on massive Q1 blowout ($10.25B rev +38%, data center +57%, Q2 guide $11.2B vs $10.5B expected). One ship transited the Strait of Hormuz under US escort — first in weeks. Oil -3.5% to $102.68 (Brent), -3.5% WTI $102.68. VIX -5% to 17.38. Goldman Sachs: AI's impact on jobs still limited to tech sector. JPMorgan raised Royal Caribbean despite Iran headwinds.
topDriver: Memory AI confirmation: Micron +11% shipping world's highest-capacity SSD, HBM sold out through 2026 — plus AMD Q1 blowout AH ($10.25B, data center +57%, Q2 guide $11.2B). AI hardware stack fully confirmed.
narrativeSummary: May 5 delivered the cleanest single-session summary of the current AI regime yet. Monday's Iran-driven selloff was a one-day panic; Tuesday confirmed it was just that. The session was driven by two overlapping AI hardware confirmations that arrived simultaneously. First: Micron began shipping the 6600 ION SSD — the world's highest-capacity storage device — driving a 10%+ surge that pushed the stock past $700B market cap for the first time. Micron's HBM products are reportedly sold out through 2026. Second, after the bell, AMD reported Q1 revenues of $10.25B — $360M above the highest estimate — with data center revenue up 57% and a Q2 guide of $11.2B, $700M above the Street's $10.5B expectation. Lisa Su said AI infrastructure demand is 'accelerating.' The AI trade is no longer just about training compute (NVDA) — it now spans the full hardware stack: memory (MU), storage (MU), CPUs (INTC, AMD), and AI GPUs (NVDA). Intel's 13% surge on Apple chip supply reports completed the picture. On the geopolitical side, one ship successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz under US military escort — the first in weeks — removing some of Monday's acute tail risk. Oil fell 3.5%, VIX dropped 5%, and yields eased 2-3bps. The ceasefire is fragile but holding. Materials surged 2% as the Monday selloff reversed. Palantir -7% despite a record earnings beat illustrated the valuation risk in over-owned names. Shopify -15% on a Q1 miss showed consumer-facing software is under pressure even as infrastructure AI soars.
macroStressSubtext: Iran truce holds + oil falls + records set; Hormuz still restricted, Warsh transition risk, ISM contraction keep regime elevated.
rateCurveRead: Yields moved sharply higher on May 5 — the 10Y rose 6bps to 4.45% and the 30Y crossed 5.00% to 5.02% for the first time since 2007, even as oil fell and the Iran truce held. The move reflects the JOLTS report (March job openings above estimates) and the continued backdrop of PCE 3.5%, ISM Manufacturing 48.7, and impending Fed transition to Warsh. The 2/10 spread widened to +50bps, the widest since 2022. The 30Y at 5.02% is a significant psychological and technical level — it reflects the fiscal risk premium that the bond market is demanding independent of the geopolitical de-escalation. The bear-steepener is structural, not transient. Source: Federal Reserve H.15, May 5, 2026 official release.

flowsRead: May 5 flows are the clearest expression yet of the AI hardware supercycle trade. The dominant inflow — $4.1B into semiconductors — reflects the full AI hardware stack being confirmed simultaneously: Micron (memory/storage), Intel (CPUs), AMD (GPU/CPU convergence). This is the trade rotating away from the AI narrative layer (Meta, MSFT) and toward the hardware reality layer (MU, INTC, AMD, and NVDA on May 20). Long-duration bond outflows of $1.2B are the most worrying signal — the 30Y crossing 5.00% was not a panic move but a steady repricing of fiscal risk independent of inflation. The bond market is telling a structural story that equities are not yet pricing.

drivers.name: AI Hardware Full Stack Confirmed — Memory, Storage, CPU all firing simultaneously
drivers.detail: May 5 is the day the AI hardware supercycle confirmed its breadth. Three simultaneous data points: Micron launched the 6600 ION — world's highest-capacity SSD — and reported HBM sold out through 2026 (+11%); Intel surged 13% on Apple chip supply discussions, validating the US semiconductor reshoring narrative; AMD after the bell reported $10.25B revenue (+38%), data center +57%, Q2 guide $11.2B vs $10.5B expected (+24.7% EBITDA beat). The Bloomberg Global Memory Index is up 500% over the past year. AICS aiRevCapexRatio now 0.88, approaching the 1.0 parity threshold. UBS sees server CPU TAM growing from $30B (2025) to $170B (2030). Nvidia May 20 is the next confirmation event.

drivers.name: Iran Ceasefire Fragile But Holding — First Hormuz Ship Transit Under US Escort
drivers.source: CNBC, Schwab Market Update, Charles Schwab, NYSE Commentary
drivers.detail: One ship successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz under US Navy escort ('Project Freedom') — the first since the blockade intensified. The ceasefire held overnight despite Monday's exchanges (Iran fired on US warships, US destroyed 6 Iranian small boats). hormuzclosurePct upgraded from 4% to 12% — still critically low but the directional signal is positive. Hegseth said the world needs American leadership to secure Hormuz and the US hopes Iran will reach a deal. Goldman maintains Hormuz at 4% normal flow structurally. The Iran peace proposal (sent via Pakistan mediators) is still on the table — Trump 'not satisfied' but back-channel active.

drivers.name: 30Y Treasury Crosses 5.00% — Fiscal Risk Premium Now Structural
drivers.detail: The 30Y Treasury yield crossed 5.02% today — the first time since 2007 — even as oil fell and equities rallied. This decoupling is the key signal: the long-end selloff is no longer just about energy inflation. It is a fiscal risk premium repricing driven by the combination of: a PCE stuck at 3.5%, a Fed in transition (Warsh June 17), a JOLTS labour market above estimates, and growing concern about the US fiscal trajectory. The 2/10 spread at +50bps is the widest since 2022. Bear-steepener is structural, not transient. TLT outflow of $1.2B confirms institutional positioning.

drivers.name: Valuation Warning — Palantir -7% on Earnings Beat Shows Over-Owned Risk
drivers.detail: Palantir reported record revenue and an earnings beat — and fell 7%. Shopify missed Q1 and fell 15.8%. These are the mirror images of the AI bifurcation: infrastructure AI rewarded, consumer-facing and over-valued AI punished. Palantir's multiple had run too far for even a clean beat to sustain. This is a forward warning for other high-multiple AI names ahead of Nvidia (May 20) — the beat needs to be massive, not just clean, to avoid a 'sell the news' reaction at 30-40x forward multiples.

drivers.name: JOLTS Above Estimates — March Job Openings Confirm Labour Market Too Tight for Warsh to Cut
drivers.source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Schwab Market Update
drivers.detail: March JOLTS job openings came in above consensus — confirming the labour market is structurally tight even as manufacturing enters contraction (ISM 48.7). Goldman Sachs research: AI's impact on jobs 'still limited to tech sector.' The broader economy is creating jobs; it's the tech layer being restructured. This combination — tight labour, sticky inflation, manufacturing contraction — is the textbook stagflation triplet. Warsh's June 17 inaugural meeting will face this backdrop. fedTransitionRisk holds at 74.

risks.title: 30Y above 5.00% — fiscal risk premium repricing could trigger equity multiple compression
risks.desc: The 30Y at 5.02% is the highest since 2007 and is rising independently of the Iran narrative. If this move continues — driven by fiscal concerns, Warsh hawkishness, or a PCE surprise — it will eventually collide with equity valuations at 25-30x forward earnings. The S&P 500 at 7,259 implies ~29x 2026 EPS. A 30Y at 5.25%+ would make that multiple very difficult to sustain.

risks.title: Ceasefire fragility — Monday's missile exchanges show how quickly truce can break
risks.desc: Monday's events (Iran fired on US warships, US destroyed 6 Iranian small boats, oil spiked 5%) happened within hours and reversed Tuesday. The speed of reversal is both reassuring and alarming — markets can go from +1% to -1% on a single headline. The ceasefire has no formal mechanism and is described as 'tenuous' by both sides. Any escalation to critical infrastructure targeting would spike Brent to $125+ immediately.

risks.title: Nvidia May 20 earnings — high-multiple valuation requires a massive beat, not just a clean one
risks.desc: Palantir's -7% on a clean earnings beat is the warning shot. Nvidia at ~35x forward earnings requires a blowout — data center revenue likely needs to exceed $45B with a Q2 guide above $50B to sustain the current multiple. AMD's Q2 guide of $11.2B (vs $10.5B expected) sets the benchmark for what a 'proper' beat looks like. A merely good Nvidia print could trigger a 5-10% pullback in the semiconductor complex.

risks.title: Shopify + Palantir divergence — consumer-facing software under real pressure
risks.desc: Two high-profile software names missed or disappointed on May 5. Shopify -15.8% on Q1 miss confirms that consumer-facing e-commerce and software are not benefiting from AI tailwinds yet. Palantir -7% on a beat shows valuation has run ahead of fundamentals. This extends the week's pattern: infrastructure AI is the only AI trade working right now. Software that is AI-adjacent but not AI-infrastructure is at risk.

risks.title: GameStop-eBay bid — corporate governance and M&A quality risk
risks.desc: GameStop submitted an unsolicited $56B offer to acquire eBay at $125/share in cash and stock. The deal is logically incoherent — a physical game retail business offering $56B for an e-commerce platform using its own stock as currency. eBay stock rose but GME fell 10% on the proposal. The offer signals GameStop is burning cash without a viable digital strategy. More broadly, the bid raises questions about the quality of M&A activity when cash-flush meme stocks attempt transformative deals.

strategies.title: Short TLT / Long TIPS — 30Y at 5.02% structural fiscal repricing
strategies.body: 30Y crossed 5.00% today independent of oil and Iran. This is fiscal risk premium + stagflation + Warsh transition. Short TLT at 5.02% 30Y yield is structurally attractive — the downside is a rapid Iran deal (Brent collapses, PCE falls) but even then the fiscal risk premium remains. TIPS capture both scenarios: if inflation stays elevated they win on real yield, if Iran resolves they win on declining nominal yields.

strategies.title: Nvidia May 20 position — size down pre-earnings given Palantir warning

AMD's $11.2B Q2 guide (vs $10.5B expected) sets the bar for what a proper beat looks like — Nvidia needs to clear it by more. Prudent to reduce position size into May 20 and re-add post-print if guide is strong.
